correctness.rationale: The beta-binomial mass q_k=P(K_k=0)>0 forces L′(0+)=+infinity; strict L″<0 and B E(P)>s force a unique finite interior optimum. Conditional Bernoulli sample means decrease strictly in convex order, so their inverse response equations force h_(k+1)<h_k. Conditional LLN and bounded derivatives yield h_k down to maximizer of the beta-mixture limit. The endpoint derivative is r-1, r=(s/B)E(P^-1). For alpha>1,r<1, split E[1/R_k]=q_k/h_k+S_k; the k/(K+1) binomial bound gives conditional domination by C/P, hence S_k->r and q_k/h_k->1-r. Gamma ratio yields the stated sharp coefficient k^-alpha. Boundary h_k=2/(k+2) and arcsine limit 1/3 follow from explicit beta-binomial and arcsine identities. These arguments cover all alpha,beta>0 and k>=1 subject to stated B E(P)>s; no universal critical rate is claimed.
